Identity: the heading 'EXECUTIVE ORDER 9998', the title and the signing date of September 14, 1948 agree with the register row. I confirmed the dossier's fifteen numbered items as the complete inventory; the lead-in sentence is the prescribing formula for those items and adds no separate command. No item has an own-terms end; item 3's proviso depends on the Foreign Assistance Act of 1948 remaining in force, whose text is not held, so that proviso is not relied on. Item 15 supersedes EO 8356 and EO 8377 and is recorded as performed on 1948-09-14. A search of the held order texts for the number 9998 finds no instrument other than the order itself, the dossier chain has no event, and the dossier lists no 'target provision not located' or conflict line. research_rationale: Blocked on a precise source gap, not on the legal merits. I read the held official text of EO 10173 (15 FR 7005, signed 1950-10-18; the preamble finding, Part 6 of 33 CFR with its definitions, enforcement, access, anchorage, identification and security provisions) and confirmed identity from the heading, title and date. The order is not a short list of commands but the text of regulations that became 33 CFR Part 6, and the later held orders rewrite them section by section: EO 10277 (1951-08-01) amends sections 6.04-1, 6.10-1 and 6.10-7 and adds subparts 6.14 and 6.19, EO 10352 (1952-05-19) and EO 11249 amend further sections, EO 13143 (1999-12-01) rewrites section 6.01-4, EO 13273 (2002-08-21) amends the regulations and EO 14116 (2024-02-21) rewrites sections 6.01-3 and 6.01-5 and adds section 6.01-7. The dossier inventory has only four coarse clauses (the first two spans cover about 12,000 characters and the third about 8,500) and would need a section-by-section override. The gap: whether each section of the original regulations still stands, was replaced, or was redesignated cannot be decided from the held bytes. The continuing text of these regulations lives in 33 CFR Part 6, but no held byte-for-byte copy of the current Part 6 (or of the Coast Guard rules that have since revised it) is registered in this packet; the current-law job outputs are leads only and cannot be quoted. Without it I cannot say, for any section the later orders do not mention, that the original wording is the wording now in force, and several later orders (EO 10352, 11249, 13273) were not resolvable one section at a time from the registered texts, so a held later instrument may have ended or replaced a clause I cannot resolve. Missing sources: the current 33 CFR Part 6 text through 2026-10-14 registered for this order, and the section-by-section dossier inventory for the original regulations.

Identity: heading, title and date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory was wrong (parts of sections 2 and 3 repeated), so I replaced it with the order's own 11 provisions (inventory override). Own terms: no section has an end date or ending condition; section 9 fixes effective dates only. Later instruments, read in full where they name the order: EO 12883 (1993-11-29) adds section 2(c); EO 13106 section 8 (1998-12-07) amends section 2(c); EO 13415 (signed 2006-12-01; Federal Register copy held) section 2(a) revokes sections 3 and 6 and renumbers sections 4, 5, 7, 8 and 9 as 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7, and its section 1 assigns presidential functions under 5 U.S.C. 4505a, 5305 and 5377 to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management. Sections 3 and 6 are therefore terminated by express revocation on 2006-12-01; the renumbering is attached as an amendment on the other clauses. EO 12764 only recites the Pay Agent of section 2(a). The dossier's 'target provision not located: EO:12764' line is resolved this way. Sections 4, 5 and 8(a) are self-executing and recorded as performed on their stated effective dates. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record no revocation or supersession of the whole order beyond EO 13415's partial revocation; the Code notes and 5 CFR parts 531 and 550 the leads point to are corroboration only and are not quoted. Limit stated plainly: continuation of sections 1, 2, 7, 8(b) and 9 rests on the original text, the attached amendments and the absence of any further ending in the bounded searches (U.S. Code edition through 2026-10-09); the statutes the order implements are not held.
savings_reason: EO 12748 has no savings clause, and EO 13415's revocation of sections 3 and 6 states none; the functions are reassigned rather than saved, so no residual effect of the revoked sections is claimed. The performed section 4, 5 and 8(a) commands leave their consequences in EO 11721, EO 10982 and Civil Service Rule 9.
